hypothesis: Can github-copilot/claude-sonnet-5 high replace github-copilot/claude-opus-5 high for Build without degrading functional correctness/invariants, while demonstrating enough operational advantage to justify changing the restored baseline?

conditional_workload.trigger: only if build-feature and build-bugfix do not produce a decision under the ordered criteria
conditional_workload.note: No fixture content exists yet for build-refactor. Authoring it, if this contingency triggers, is separate follow-up work not covered by this preflight's budget.

initial_sample.deviation_from_3_pair_default: Deviates from the task brief's own suggested 3-pair shape, not from the repository's design: the governing decision doc has no 3-pair default. Its own sections 20.2 and 24 already list build-feature/build-bugfix as Required and build-refactor as Conditional, run only if the first two do not produce a decision. build-refactor also has no fixture content yet.

invalid_attempt_replacement_rule: pair-level: if either arm of a pair is classified INVALID_ENVIRONMENT, the entire pair is discarded and replaced with a fresh pair (both arms redispatched) to preserve paired comparability, not just the affected arm.

secondary_observational_criterion.reason: Frozen threshold requires a >2194.8831% relative-range separation to count as a real difference; historical Build cost variance alone (23.19-26.19 credits across 3 Opus runs) cannot plausibly clear this. Cost is recorded and reported, never used to declare a winner.

functional_regression.condition: Sonnet is worse than Opus on any earlier-priority functional criterion (1-5) on either workload
functional_regression.note: Operational advantages cannot compensate. Adjudication stops here.

functional_improvement.condition: Sonnet is strictly better under the earliest differentiating functional criterion (1-5) and is not worse on the other workload under any earlier-or-equal-priority functional criterion
functional_improvement.note: Wall-clock superiority is not required in this case.

functional_tie.condition: criteria 1-5 are functionally tied across both workloads
functional_tie.decision_rule: Sonnet may be adopted only if it demonstrates the precommitted wall-clock advantage on BOTH workloads independently, using the exact wall-clock comparison formula already committed above (primary_operational_advantage_threshold) -- not reinterpreted or recomputed

required.build-feature: Sonnet exceeds threshold in the favorable direction
required.build-bugfix: Sonnet exceeds threshold in the favorable direction

functional_tie.aggregation: none -- both workloads must independently clear the threshold; no averaging, no one-workload win compensating for a non-win on the other

final_adoption_rule.cost: observational only -- cannot trigger adoption under any branch of this rule
final_adoption_rule.wall_clock_threshold_caveat: 37.8885% is a precommitted minimum practical effect derived from Phase-0 self-variance on a different fixture family (github-copilot/gpt-5.6-luna). It is not a statistical-significance threshold and is not claimed to characterize Build-specific latency variance (Build's own historical range is 10.7%-1081.5% depending on cold-cache inclusion -- see the decision doc). Requiring both workloads to clear it independently is the additional protection against a one-workload timing outlier. The timing harness is not hardened further before execution.

historical_budgets.note: Closed, not reused, not reset, not enlarged. Phase 3 uses a new, separate budget.

sonnet_cost_per_run.source: no live Sonnet Build history exists; estimated via a pricing ratio derived from two directly comparable, same-shape capability-preflight probes (single-turn, ~18.1-18.2k tokens each, same provider, same standard pricing regime): eval/records/phase-r/preflight/build.json (opus, cost 0.11422875) and eval/records/claude-sonnet-5-high.json (sonnet, cost 0.045259)
sonnet_cost_per_run.uncertainty: This ratio is derived from single-turn trivial calls, not multi-turn agentic Build tasks. If Sonnet requires materially more turns/retries to solve the same task, its total cost could exceed this estimate despite a lower per-token rate. The conservative ceiling therefore assumes NO Sonnet cost savings (priced at Opus's own historical maximum).

derivation.initial_4_dispatches_ceiling: 4 x 26.192 (opus max, no Sonnet savings assumed) = 104.77
derivation.replacement_allowance: 1 additional complete paired comparison (2 dispatches) priced at the Opus historical ceiling = 52.38
